title: 100 ac Land at Lolldaiga Valley
description:
Lolldaiga Valley is a 3,750 acre area of private land in the beautiful Lolldaiga Hills in Laikipia, Kenya. The area enjoys stunning views of Mount Kenya and supports wildlife such as lion, cheetah, leopard, African wild dog, giraffe and elephant with a high diversity of plant species. The Western Plains North plot is opportunity to build a home in nature and be part of an inspiring, environmentally driven vision to protect and restore this landscape.

Situated just 30 minutes from Nanyuki, Lolldaiga Valley enjoys a malaria-free environment at an elevation of 6,000 feet, boasting a delightful climate with warm days and cool nights. Accessible by a scenic 3.5-hour drive from Nairobi or 45 minutes by air, the valley is nestled amidst renowned wildlife conservation areas, offering numerous nature and adventure activities and shared access to a network of over 40km of walking trails across the wider Lolldaiga Valley area.

Western Plains North comprises 100 acres of low-lying forest, grasslands and a spectacular ridgeline, with superb views of Mount Kenya and across the plains of Laikipia. The plot offers excellent wildlife viewing and wonderful views over the neighbouring Lolldaiga Conservancy. The land features a private trail network and numerous superb sundowner spots on the ridgeline.

The plot features low-lying acacia woodland in the west, with a large, wildlife-rich grassland plain rising in the east to the ridgeline, with fascinating rock features and amazing views in all directions. There are habitat restoration opportunities available to further enhance forest cover and possibilities to maximise wildlife viewing through a series of small waterholes and hides on the fringes of the woodland.

The Lolldaiga Valley initiative is offering long-term leases or licences (99 years automatically renewable) over each plot, with a modest annual contribution to management costs, habitat restoration and community programmes thereafter.  Service charges for items such as water, track and trail maintenance and security will be levied on an annual basis.  A full property management service will be available for owners.

title: 30.3 ac Land at Lolldaiga Valley
description:
Lolldaiga Valley is a 3,750 acre area of private land in the beautiful Lolldaiga Hills in Laikipia, Kenya. The area enjoys stunning views of Mount Kenya and supports wildlife such as lion, cheetah, leopard, African wild dog, giraffe and elephant with a high diversity of plant species. The Western Rise North plot is opportunity to build a home in nature and be part of an inspiring, environmentally driven vision to protect and restore this landscape.

Situated just 30 minutes from Nanyuki, Lolldaiga Valley enjoys a malaria-free environment at an elevation of 6,000 feet, boasting a delightful climate with warm days and cool nights. Accessible by a scenic 3.5-hour drive from Nairobi or 45 minutes by air, the valley is nestled amidst renowned wildlife conservation areas, offering numerous nature and adventure activities and shared access to a network of over 20km of walking trails in the western zone of Lolldaiga Valley.

Western Rise North comprises 30 acres of low-lying forest and small glades, with superb views of Mount Kenya and towards the western ridgeline of Lolldaiga Valley. The plot offers a variety of habitat types and sundowner spots on the western elevations.

The plot features low-lying woodland in the west, with a series of open glades leading to a small valley with numerous game trails. The land then rises in the east to the ridgeline, with fascinating rock features and great views to Mount Kenya and the Aberdares. There are habitat restoration opportunities available to further enhance forest and grassland cover. The plot is in the western part of Lolldaiga Valley, easily accessible from the western access gate and conveniently located for the network of communal trails in the western zone.

The Lolldaiga Valley initiative is offering long-term leases or licences (99 years automatically renewable) over each plot, with a modest annual contribution to management costs, habitat restoration and community programmes thereafter.  Service charges for items such as water, track and trail maintenance and security will be levied on an annual basis.  A full property management service will be available for owners.
* There are also some architectural plans for the plot that can be shared with prospective parties.

The land is located in Narok County approximately 30 kilometers along the road connecting

primary economic activities in Narok County are agriculture, tourism and trade.
Agriculture includes mostly livestock farming, and growing of different types of crops. These are
major sources of income for residents, with many households relying on them.
Maasai Mara Game Reserve in the area attracts numerous tourists worldwide as major tourism
destination, particularly during the Great Wildebeest migration. The county is actively involved
in tourism development and promotion through initiatives like the Maasai Mara Wildlife
Conservation Association (MMWCA).
Trade also plays a significant role in the local economy. Narok town is a major trading hub, with
various businesses and markets operating within the county. Trade activities include the sale of
agriculture products, livestock, and also other unrelated goods.
In the past, this land was used for farming horticulture, avocado and grazing which has since
been abandoned. The farming relied on irrigation from the river and two dams that are on the
land. Farming still remains a very viable use for the land.
Other developments available are a farm office, a working irrigation equipment room and
tractors. The entire land has irrigation pipes connected to 75% of the land.
Besides farming, the land is ideal for hospitality investments to serve travelers to Bomet, Masai
Mara Game Reserve, Kericho and other areas in Western and Nyanza regions.
The land has access to many resources such as:
1) River water that feeds two dams that irrigate the whole land 24/7.
2) It fronts major highway from Narok to Bomet and provides easy transport of the farm
produce to the local and export markets.
3) A 3-phase power line to run the irrigation system and secure the entire land with an electric fence

title: Land in Kikuyu Town
description:
The 3 acres are about 1.5 kilometers from Kikuyu town and 700 meters off the Southern bypass. Kikuyu town is 20 kilometers to the North West of Nairobi CBD. With the Southern bypass cutting through Kikuyu, and being the only town from Mombasa Road to Waiyaki Highway, it is poised for greater and speedy growth in near future. 

Kikuyu is a sub-county town in Kiambu County which grew from a settlement of colonial missionaries. Approximately 2 kilometers from the land, are historical Presbyterian Church establishments such as The First Church - Watson chapel, educational institutions, Kikuyu Hospital and other missionary establishments dating back to the 1890’s. 

Due to geology and rich soil texture, the economic activities are livestock keeping, crops farming and trade. Kikuyu town has turned into a major commercial hub with banks, supermarkets, National Government and Sub-County offices. Inflow of the middle class investing in residential and commercial land in Kikuyu town and its environs has made it one of the fastest growing towns in Kiambu county. 

Due to the 3 acres proximity to Kikuyu town, most of the roads serving the area are tarmacked. It is a serene green leafy and wooded environment. The land is well drained with red soil and infrastructures such as electricity and community water connections. It is ideal for residential housing schemes and farming.

title: Land in Isinya
description:
This 47 acre piece is located 6 kilometers from Isinya town, along Pipeline road (which connects Isinya town to Kiserian town), and then 1.5 kilometers off Pipeline road. The economic activities within this area are agriculture and livestock herding. The land is fertile with a functional borehole. 

 

The indigenous people owning large parcels of land are mainly pastoralists and herders. None indigenous Kenyans from other regions and foreigners who have purchased land around Isinya specialize in horticulture farming for local markets in Nairobi city, its environs and the export markets. 

 

Isinya / Kiserian (Pipeline Road) are warming up to take the place that is held by Juja and Ruiru townships, on the other side of the Nairobi metropolitan area. Isinya and Kiserian are among the top economic arteries of the county, with great interest in land, which was previously grazing land, by investors who are subsequently turning the area into a profitable hub.

 

About 10 years ago after land in Athi River, Kitengela and Ongata Rongai started becoming too expensive and scarce, land buying companies shifted to Isinya and Kiserian. This has transformed the area and also brought in visitors who have commercialized the towns, and other shopping centers along Pipeline Road economically. 

 

Middle class citizens are eager to invest in small parcels of land in the outskirts of Nairobi, and are increasingly turning to urban farming in greenhouses. The new settlers are influencing infrastructure development and markets in the areas where they sell and buy farm products. 

 

The land demand along Pipeline Road has gone up compared to land in other areas within Nairobi metropolitan driving the prices higher.
